_source: Copied by hand from notebooks_models/5-final_model_comparison.ipynb and 4-category_propensity_model.ipynb saved outputs on 2026-11-03. Update by hand if the models are retrained.

repeat_purchase.target: Customer buys again within 90 days of the cutoff (2011-09-10)
repeat_purchase._scoring_model_note: TEMPORARY: scores currently come from Gradient Boosting. The team chose Random Forest as the final model; switch when its scores file is ready (see spec 001 section 8).

feature_importance._method: Permutation importance on the test set: drop in ROC-AUC when the feature is shuffled

direction._method: Logistic regression coefficients on standardised features. Positive = more likely to buy again.

threshold_tradeoff._method: Final model on the test set at different probability cut-offs

category_propensity.target: Customer buys from the category in the quarter after the cutoff
category_propensity._scoring_model_note: Notebook 4 marks version A as best; the export uses whichever network was trained last. Only customers with purchases before the cutoff are scored (3,349).
category_propensity._recall_at_5: Share of the categories a customer actually bought that were in the model's top 5 guesses

limitations: One UK gift retailer, Dec 2010 to Dec 2011, many customers are wholesalers. Results may not carry over to other businesses.
One time window that includes the Christmas peak, so probabilities are likely too optimistic. Use them to rank customers, not as exact chances.
Small test set (about 670 customers). Differences of a few points between models are within noise.
Prediction is not causation. The model predicts who will buy again, not who will buy because of marketing. Use A/B tests to measure campaign impact.
Only customers with a CustomerID are included (about 25% of rows had none). Brand-new customers can't be scored.
Country was excluded from the features to avoid targeting by nationality.
